jobs.name: loch-ness
jobs.prompt: Create one photorealistic miniature specimen icon for a museum collection displayed on a purple wall. The attached old icon is a subject/material reference only; replace its steep isometric camera. NEW CAMERA: directly from above, almost orthographic, map-like top view with very slight relief depth visible along lower/right edges. Soft strong upper-left/front light, darker right/bottom relief, restrained violet bounce. Crisp readable silhouette at small chart size. Object alone detached in space, true transparent PNG, no cast shadow, no floor, no wall, no surrounding scenery, no pedestal, no labels. Square canvas; longest solid extent 92–94%, centered, generous safe clear margin. Physically tangible miniature with fine texture, not a flat map graphic. SUBJECT: the water volume of Loch Ness alone, imagined as a delicate 3D-printed translucent deep-blue resin casting. An extremely long narrow Scottish lake planform, southwest end lower-left and northeast end upper-right; gently irregular realistic shoreline with small coves, very slight sinuousness, no branching rivers. Keep its famously slender ribbon-like proportions, not a broad oval or teardrop. No land, hills, vegetation, rocks, banks or rectangular tile. The perimeter is the lake shoreline itself. A shallow bevel and slender darker blue resin sidewall, small-scale natural water ripples on the top, fine cool specular glints, transparent blue/cobalt depths with a restrained violet undertone that harmonizes with #433193. Subtle depth variations convey a cast water body. No interior bright caustic net overwhelming the lake, no floating bubbles or fish. The long narrow lake runs diagonally to use the square canvas.
